line: This is the AI engine our go-to-market runs on. Everything you are about to see is live.
Five places we already look, from Salesforce to the market signals, feed one AI engine.
The AI takes current customers out, writes the sequence for everyone cleared, and a reply lands back in Salesforce as a meeting.
Inside the engine, six steps. The AI runs most of them itself. Two places a person still decides, and those are the two that keep us safe.
Act one. A rep, a target account, and a blank page.

One ask, in plain English. The AI reads the public record, names the buying committee, and writes a ten-day plan: emails, LinkedIn notes and voicemails for every person on it, in the rep's voice. Every signal on screen carries its date and its source. This is what Nate and the sales team run from today.
It carries the rules with it: what is verified, who is excluded, and how to answer the pushback before it comes.
[ Nothing. Let the card land. ]
Act two. Our customers' front offices know us. Their back offices don't.

So we went and found them. Everyone we know, in one place, synced from Salesforce. A hundred and forty thousand people. Then one saved filter: back-office leaders, director and up, inside accounts we already serve. Three hundred and twelve people who have never heard from us. That used to be a week of exports and spreadsheets. It costs nothing and it stays current on its own.

For every one of them: verify the email, read what they have said publicly, find which contact center platforms their company runs, and pull the persona and the angle. Here is that research running on ten people at once.
[ Say nothing. Nine seconds. The screen carries it. ]
Then the AI writes the first touch for each person from exactly this, and every draft passes a fact check before it moves.

Then the AI turns names into the org. When the account management team needed back-office maps for their strategic accounts, it sourced the people, checked every name against Salesforce, and delivered them as a live page. This is MetLife: the senior executive at the top, the lanes underneath, who reports up to whom. Eighteen accounts so far, and the account manager clears every name before a word goes out.

And inside every org there is a buying committee. We used to sell to one person. Now we sell to four: the economic buyer, the evaluator, the champion, and the integration owner. Here is State Farm's. This is the targeting standard now.
[ Nothing. Let the card land. ]
Act three. The rep has the people and the drafts. Running them is the job.

So that is automated too. Cleared contacts land here. Email, LinkedIn and a call step per person, on a cadence. Every line you are reading was drafted by the AI for this individual, at this company, this week. The rep owns the send, and every reply comes back to them. Seven campaigns are sending today across North America and the UK.
[ Nothing. Let the card land. ]
It doesn't stop at outbound. Alliances asked, and the same AI answered.
Account research and a follow-up one-pager per partner account. Two AI skills build both in about five minutes, and Frank runs them himself.
Public sources, read on the day, with the gaps named rather than filled.
Who to talk to, where each name came from, and what still needs a live check before it reaches a sequence.
And the one-pager that follows, built from that company's own filings. The same AI routed a thousand webinar registrants in a week.
One AI engine. It runs work like this for any team.
